messages:
pagerduty-bot: [ALERT] p99 inference latency spike in az1a - multiple 5xx and token stalls reported. Triggered by path: inference-hosts/az1a - severity: potential customer impact

mira: I'm on it. confirming whether this is network or instance-level. grabbing console logs and tcpdump.

kai: seeing increased egress retransmits from g5 instances in az1a, lots of RSTs to external NAT IPs. metrics: ENI TX errors up ~300% at 16:02 UTC.

nico: NAT Gateway metrics show high active flows and high SNAT allocation churn. Could be NAT saturation + asymmetric path causing conn resets.

sam: runtime telemetry shows KV cache misses spike and kvcache stall logs: "kvcache: stream stalled waiting for network_write" — this looks downstream.

jess: Support is getting incoming tickets about generation failures (502) and timeouts from 3 paying customers on Dedicated capacity. Notified CSMs.

incbot: Incident created (INC-2064829999), priority: P1 (customer-visible), owner: mira. Runbook: az-egress-network-degradation.

mira: Quick plan: 1) divert new requests to eu1/uw2 model variants (safe fallback) 2) attempt to reduce egress from az1a by draining non-critical background workload 3) if NAT gw still saturated, create temporary NAT in different subnet or move Egress via transit-gw to eu1.

kai: I'll start a traffic steering canary: update smart-routing policy to prefer eu1 for non-low-latency-tier traffic and route 30% of inference tail to eu1. Doing now.

(devops-bot) deploy-bot: route-policy update submitted: smart-routing:az1a->eu1 (weight 30%). CID: rp-48f2.

sam: Can we reduce parallelism on live hosts to lower conn churn? I'll patch the serving config to drop max_concurrency from 64 -> 32 for affected pool g5-az1a-inference-01. Pushing patch.

nico: Created alternate NAT (nat-aux-az1a-02) in private subnet and attached to ELB egress path. If we can switch host egress SNAT to nat-aux, should relieve the main NAT.

mira: Command to reassign route table for egress (run from infra bastion):
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-az1a-egress --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-aux-az1a-02
```
Will run after coordination with security (changing egress).

kai: Observability note: dns resolver latency also jumped ~40ms -> could be packet loss to resolver; adding retry/backoff to client side could help, but that's longer fix.

mira: Running the replace-route now (will monitor for connection thrash).

devops-bot: Route replace initiated by mira@infra-bastion; request id r-0a7c.

(5m later) mira: Route swap completed. Early signs: ENI TX errors dropping, retransmits falling. Observation windows: p50 latency back near baseline; p95 improving but still elevated.

sam: After reducing concurrency and route swap, token stall errors decreased by ~70% for routed traffic. We still see periodic bursts of 502s for some sticky sessions (long-lived connections).

nico: Also rebalanced some outbound flows across the aux NAT. Active flows on nat-main dropped from 16k -> 3.1k. nat-aux is at 6.8k and stable.

jess: Sent customer update: "We've identified an egress network issue in az1a causing intermittent generation failures. We've routed most traffic to other regions and applied mitigations. We're monitoring and will follow up." Customers acknowledged.

mira: Next: prefer soft-failover policy changes to avoid DNS TTL churn. We'll keep route_rules for 30% to eu1 and gradually increase if stable. Also plan to avoid full DNS flip.

incbot: Update: Severity remains P1 while impact persists; mitigation in flight. Handoff scheduled to kai for next 1-hr watch.

mira: Handoff to kai — summary: NAT saturation + asymmetric egress -> conn resets -> kvcache stalls -> token 502s. Mitigations applied: decrease concurrency on pool, route-table swap to aux NAT, routing policy canary to eu1. Watch metrics: ENI TX errs, nat-active-flows, kvcache-stall-rate, p99-token-latency.

kai: Taking over. I'll keep 1:1 with support and infra. Also starting scrub to identify if a single tenant flow was the cause (large outbound connections).

(20m later) kai: Monitoring shows continued small tail spikes correlated with a single backend IP (54.23.11.77) — looks like a telemetry exporter from a partner is hammering egress. Blocking that IP via NACL for now.

nico: NACL deny applied on rtb-subnet-az1a -> blocked 54.23.11.77. Conn spikes stopped for that vector.

sam: Noting that some long-lived websocket sessions to customers' clients are sticky and may need graceful reconnects. Pushing a hotfix to do websocket reconnect with jitter.

jess: Support: 2 customers report improved experience; 1 still sees elevated p99s (heavy inference flows, Dedicated). Escalating to solutions team for white-glove migration to eu1 for their critical routes.

kai: Metrics look stable for 12m. nat-main active flows steady <4k, kvcache stall rate <1%. Marking mitigation succeeded but keeping incident open for postmortem.

incbot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to P2. Assigned postmortem to mira & kai.

mira: Actions for postmortem: 1) quantify customer impact (#requests failed, affected customers + SLO miss window) 2) improve smart-routing automated fallback to do region-level fast-fail instead of slow-canary when nat saturation heuristics detected 3) add egress capacity alarms and automated aux-nat failover 4) runbook updates for NACL quick block and websocket reconnect guidance.

jess: I'll draft customer follow-up with timelines and remediation steps.

kai: Thanks everyone. If anything pops up, @kai is primary for the next hour. I'll also schedule a quick incident review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Incident INC-2064829999 annotated: mitigations applied (route-swap, concurrency-reduction, aux-nat, nacl-block).

mira: closing handoff.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2064829999 status changed to MONITORING - assigned to kai.
